To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) fluid reabsorption in the proximal tubule of uremic rabbits is increased, and 2) this increase is closely correlated with the compensatory hypertrophy which occurs in the uremic remant kidney.

fluid reabsorptive capacity per unit length of superficial proximal straight renal tubule is increased by approximately 70% in the remnant kidney of the uremic rabbit and that this functional change is closely correlated with hypertrophy of the tubular segment.

the superficial proximal straight (PCT-like) tubules of the remnant kidney in uremia are functionally adapted to increase fluid reabsorption in proportion to the degree of hypertrophy of these tubules, and that this functional change does not appear to be dependent upon a uremically altered peritubular milieu.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the functional and metabolic alterations in the isolated perfused nephron.
the study of single tubular function in the uremic remanent kidney.
the pathogenesis of the uremic syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the proximal straight segment of the uremic nephron, there is a marked increase in fluid reabsorption which is closely correlated to compensatory hypertrophy.

the functional profile of the isolated PST in uremia differs from that of the normal tubule in that there is a marked increase in fluid reabsorption which is closely correlated with the degree of compensatory hypertrophic growth.
the isolated superficial PST of the remnant kidney of the uremic rabbit is capable of adapting to its altered environment in such a way as to increase its capacity for fluid absorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superficial proximal straight segment is the site of increased fluid reabsorption in the uremic remanant kidney and this is due to compensatory hypertrophy.

the functional profile of the isolated nephron in uremia is characterized by: 1) increased reabsorption of sodium and water by the superficial PST; and 2) increased secretion of bicarbonate and potassium by the superficial PST and the superficial distal tubule.

the superficial proximal straight (PST) tubule of the remnant kidney of the uremic rabbit exhibits compensatory hypertrophy and an increased rate of fluid re-absorption which is not influenced by the uremic milieu.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uremic kidney is a unique and interesting organ.
the proximal straight segment of the nephron is the major site of fluid reabsorbtion in the kidney and that it is the segment that is affected most by uremia.
the proximal straight segment of the nephron in uremia is hypertrophied and that this is associated with an increase in the rate of fluid re-absorption.
